Welcome to the Iwate Prefectural Fisheries Science Museum! Iwate Prefecture is part of the Sanriku Offshore Fishing Grounds, and fishing is thriving here. However, valuable cultural heritage was gradually being lost. In response, in 1986, the prefecture invested approximately 800 million yen and opened a prefectural science museum specializing in fisheries in Jodogahama, the central area of the Sanriku Reconstruction National Park.
In the entrance hall, we have 17 tanks showcasing a variety of seafood, with a focus on fish from the Miyako area. Marine fish from the Sanriku region, as well as Yamame, Iwana, and tropical fish, are all on display, generously provided by local fishermen.
This science museum was established to preserve and pass on the fishing culture of Iwate Prefecture. We invite you to explore the charm of the sea in Sanriku and delve into the history of fishing, gaining insights into the local culture. Please enjoy your visit!

The waters off the coast of Iwate Prefecture are home to nearly 500 species of fish. In the seaweed beds near the shore, schools of sand lances and sculpins gather, while smaller fish like rockfish and gobies make appearances. In sandy or muddy areas, flounders and flatfish hunt for prey. Rocky areas serve as hiding spots for flatheads, sculpins, and blennies.
Offshore, you can find salmon, cherry salmon, masu salmon, and hokke, as well as migratory species like Japanese pilchard, tuna, and Pacific saury. In deeper waters, there are luminescent lanternfish and foxface rabbitfish. Due to global warming, fish that were traditionally found south of the Kanto region are now being caught in these waters as well. Our aquarium showcases this diverse array of fish. We hope you enjoy the exhibit!
